epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. Each exported row contains the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded, and the file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and the encoding of the file are not yet decided.

features.description: Single capability allowing a customer to download their paid orders as a CSV file from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer is on their account page, When they trigger the export action, Then a CSV file is delivered to them as a download.
Given a customer has no paid orders, When they trigger the export action, Then a CSV file is still produced and contains no order rows.
Given a customer triggers the export, When the file is generated, Then it contains only that customer's orders.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story is implementable: a trigger action on the account page delivers a CSV download restricted to the connected customer's own orders, and the empty-result case is defined (a CSV with no order rows).
stories.description: The account page offers an action that starts the export of the customer's paid orders and delivers the resulting CSV file to the customer. Only the connected customer's own orders are concerned. The content of the file is covered by other stories.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases outside the website

tasks.description: Add an action on the customer's account page that starts the export of their paid orders. Expected result: a customer on the account page can trigger the export action.
tasks.title: Add the export trigger action to the account page

tasks.description: Implement the server-side handling of the export request so that it is only accepted for the connected customer. Expected result: a trigger from an authenticated customer starts generation of the export for that customer's paid orders.
tasks.title: Implement the backend export trigger for the connected customer

tasks.description: Return the generated CSV file to the requesting customer as a file download. When the customer has no paid orders, still produce a CSV file that contains no order rows. Expected result: the customer receives a CSV download, including the empty-file case.
tasks.title: Deliver the generated CSV file to the customer as a download

tasks.description: Write automated tests that check the three acceptance criteria: a CSV is delivered as a download from the account page, an empty CSV is produced for a customer without paid orders, and the file only contains the connected customer's orders. Expected result: the tests pass and cover each criterion.
tasks.title: Verify the export trigger, download and customer scoping

stories.title: Trigger CSV export of paid orders from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer has two paid orders, When the export is generated, Then the file contains exactly two order rows.
Given an order, When its row is exported, Then the row contains its order number, its date and its total amount including VAT.
Given the export is generated, When the file is read, Then the content uses the delimiter and encoding decided by the Product Owner.
stories.aiReadyReason: The acceptance criteria require the delimiter and encoding 'decided by the Product Owner', but they are not decided, so a developer cannot choose them alone. Which delimiter (comma or semicolon) and which encoding should the exported CSV use?
dependencies: Trigger CSV export of paid orders from account page
stories.description: The CSV file contains one row per paid order with three values: order number, date and total amount including VAT. The delimiter (comma or semicolon) and the encoding of the file are not decided. The format of the date is not specified.
stories.iWant: each paid order to appear as one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can see the key figures of each order in the exported file
stories.title: Export one row per paid order with required columns

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer has one paid order and one cancelled order, When the export is generated, Then only the paid order appears in the file.
Given a customer has only cancelled orders, When the export is generated, Then the file contains no order rows.
Given a cancelled order exists, When the export is generated, Then no row for that order is present in the file.
stories.aiReadyReason: The rule is clear: cancelled orders are excluded from the file and non-cancelled paid orders are included, and each criterion can be checked directly against that rule.
dependencies: Export one row per paid order with required columns
stories.description: Orders that have been cancelled do not appear in the exported file. Paid orders that are not cancelled are included.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the exported file only lists orders that are valid for me

tasks.description: Filter out cancelled orders when generating the export, while keeping paid orders that are not cancelled. Expected result: the generated file contains no row for any cancelled order.
tasks.title: Exclude cancelled orders from the export generation

tasks.description: Write automated tests for the three acceptance criteria: a paid order is kept while a cancelled order is removed, a customer with only cancelled orders gets a file with no order rows, and no row for a cancelled order is present. Expected result: the tests pass and cover each criterion.
tasks.title: Verify exclusion of cancelled orders from the export

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from the export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer triggers the export, When the file is downloaded, Then its name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
Given the file name is generated, When it is checked, Then it ends with the .csv extension.
Given the file name is generated, When it is checked, Then the date part uses the four-digit year, two-digit month and two-digit day.
stories.aiReadyReason: The date used to fill YYYY-MM-DD in the file name is explicitly left open, so the developer cannot pick it alone. Which date should fill the YYYY-MM-DD part of the file name: the export date or another date?
dependencies: Trigger CSV export of paid orders from account page
stories.description: The downloaded file is named with the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The specification does not state which date fills the YYYY-MM-DD part (export date or another date), so this is left open.
stories.iWant: the downloaded file to be named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
stories.soThat: I can identify my order export easily
stories.title: Name exported file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
